name: Andrew Cuomo
role: Governor of New York (2011-2021); state attorney general (2007-2010); US HUD secretary (1997-2001); 2025 New York City mayoral candidate
summary: Andrew Cuomo is a Democrat whose record combines progressive social and labor measures with fiscal restraint and a tough-on-crime posture. As governor he signed marriage equality, the SAFE Act gun law, a $15 minimum wage, paid family leave and climate legislation, while capping property taxes and restraining spending. In his 2025 mayoral run he stressed policing, housing supply and opposition to higher taxes on the wealthy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Mixed: in 2017 he called the federal Medicare for All plan a good idea and a state single-payer system an exciting possibility, but later voiced cost concerns; he also codified ACA protections and expanded Medicaid.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Proposed and secured a statewide minimum wage rising to $15 and called the current wage unlivable; 2025 platform proposed $20.

public-ownership.rationale: Rejects the socialist platform (free buses, rent freeze) as failing when tried; favors 'private enterprise with guardrails'.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Mixed: he signed a 2011 tax increase on high earners (extended to 2027) and in 2021 said the wealthy should pay more, but in 2025 warned that doubling taxes on the wealthy would drive them away.

unions-good.rationale: Wrote that labor unions protect fairness at the bargaining table and signed a 2018 law protecting public-sector union membership after Janus, which he called devastating to unions.

cut-welfare.rationale: Described the social safety net as a moral imperative and expanded SNAP outreach, though his book also urged earlier welfare reform; evidence leans against cutting welfare.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Cannabis legalization and specific drug scheduling are nearby; no stated position on legalizing recreational drugs generally.

state-harmful.rationale: Said government is not an alien being, it is us, and that he believes in the collective model.

limit-guns.rationale: Signed the NY SAFE Act in 2013 with an assault weapons ban, magazine limits and expanded background checks, and later backed red flag laws.

empower-police-military.rationale: 2025 platform: 5,000 more NYPD officers, retention bonuses, more subway presence; said cutting police raises crime. As governor he also ordered police reform plans.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: In a 2025 debate he attacked an opponent's stance on prostitution as making it legal for prostitutes.

rehabilitation.rationale: Funded college courses in prisons, proposed sentence reductions for rehabilitative programming and raised the age of juvenile jurisdiction.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Led the push for and signed the 2011 Marriage Equality Act; said the state finally tore down the barrier.

abortion-legal.rationale: Said it is her body, her choice, signed the 2019 Reproductive Health Act and proposed writing Roe v. Wade rights into the state constitution.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Set a 20 percent minority and women business contracting goal and framed cannabis legalization as ending the disproportionate impact on communities of color.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Said New York should stand up for immigrants and in 2025 backed lawful immigration as a city of immigrants, while saying criminals should not be harbored.

open-borders.rationale: Criticized opening the borders with no plan, while also supporting lawful immigration and the state DREAM Act.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Launched a Green New Deal, set a goal of 100 percent clean power by 2040 and signed the 2019 climate law.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Mixed: he secured the closure of Indian Point as unsafe but said the state must support upstate nuclear plants.

central-planning.rationale: Says socialism has not succeeded anywhere and that Americans do not want to dismantle the economic system; calls for 'responsible capitalism'.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Directed state funds toward chosen sectors through Regional Economic Development Councils, the NY Green Bank, Buffalo investment and tax-free innovation zones.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Wrote that the best teacher is practice rather than theory.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In 2024 and 2025 said true friends fight for the state of Israel and rejected 'occupation' language as meaning Israel has no right to exist as a Jewish state.

school-vouchers.rationale: An education tax credit for non-public tuition is nearby; no stated position on vouchers.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Championed the Women's Equality Act, pay equity law and equal treatment for women.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Banned high-volume fracking, pledged to end coal use and set a goal of 100 percent clean power.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His record is of an activist state: paid family leave, minimum wage, rent law, free tuition and public investment, and he describes government as the collective.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said Marriage Equality's passage affirmed that all New Yorkers are equal under the law and pushed antidiscrimination laws.

death-penalty.rationale: Proposed formally abolishing the death penalty in 2019, calling it archaic and discriminatory, and said his father believed state-sanctioned killing appealed to our worst impulses.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Proposed requiring comprehensive, medically accurate sex education including consent in grades 6 through 12.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Held off fracking pending a Health Department study and then prohibited it citing health risks.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Said in his 2012 State of the State that a flat tax is not a fair tax and added brackets for middle-class and high earners.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Signed marriage equality, said clerks unable to issue licenses should leave the job, ordered state travel bans on states with anti-LGBT laws, and pledged not to stand for discrimination.

corporate-influence.rationale: Described Citizens United as unleashing a torrent of dark money that drowns out ordinary voices and pushed to close the LLC loophole in campaign finance.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Proposed comprehensive reform of the Freedom of Information Law to improve transparency, including extending it to the Legislature.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Proposed passing the Gender Identity and Expression Non-Discrimination Act, regulations protecting transgender people and easier ID changes, and support for transgender troops.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Signed 2018 law limiting nondisclosure agreements and mandatory arbitration in sexual harassment cases, then proposed extending those protections.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Criticized Don't Ask, Don't Tell for discrimination against LGBTQ veterans and proposed supporting transgender troops.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Said that cutting police leads to more crime and pledged 5,000 more officers.

term-limits.rationale: Proposed a constitutional amendment imposing eight-year term limits on legislators and limits for statewide officials.

rent-control.rationale: Signed 2019 law that strengthened rent regulation and called it the greatest expansion in four decades; in 2025 he opposed a rent freeze but promised stricter enforcement of rent stabilization.

free-public-college.rationale: Created the Excelsior Scholarship making SUNY and CUNY tuition free for families under an income cap, which is partial rather than universal.

future-generations.rationale: Said it is vital to commit to a greener future to preserve natural beauty for children and grandchildren.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Proposed a Middle Class Child Care Tax Credit and made the non-custodial earned income tax credit permanent.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Called the Janus ruling, which barred mandatory agency fees for public workers, devastating to unions and signed a law to protect union membership.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Created the NY Council on Women and Girls in 2017 and used it for initiatives on pay equity and student debt.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Representing Netanyahu against specific ICC warrants is nearby; no stated position on international trials in general.

notes:
Positions rest mainly on his State of the State books (2016, 2017, 2019, 2020), compiled quotes from his books and speeches, and 2025 campaign coverage. Earlier State of the State addresses (2011-2015, 2018, 2021) and his books were not available as full text. Positions on taxes on the wealthy and on cannabis changed or were mixed over time.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 2 answers taken from it, 16 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: His father Mario Cuomo's positions are not used. Most recent position wins on taxes (he signed higher rates on top earners in 2011 and 2021 but opposes 'tax the rich' in 2026). The campaign-site op-ed text was read through a summarizing fetch tool. NYT and governor.ny.gov pages were not reachable, so governor-era laws rest on his own record page, the state program page and Wikipedia.
